name: Fewest triangles in graphs with 16 vertices and 68 edges
description: construct() -> exactly 68 distinct edges [u, v] on vertices 0..15. The score is the exact number of triangles. Minimize; the proven optimum is 32 = t * floor(n/2) with t = 68 - 64. With n = 16 and t = 4 the theorem gives at least 32 triangles, and K8,8 plus a 4-edge matching attains 32.

sources.locator: László Lovász and Miklós Simonovits, On the number of complete subgraphs of a graph II (1983). Crossref record inspected; Erdős Problem #1010 page inspected: every graph with floor(n^2/4)+t edges, t < floor(n/2), has at least t*floor(n/2) triangles, proved independently by Lovász-Simonovits and Nikiforov-Khadzhiivanov. With n = 16 and t = 4 the theorem gives at least 32 triangles, and K8,8 plus a 4-edge matching attains 32.
